issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Currently, the only way to update the RAG knowledge base is to manually place .md files in the actions/ directory and call POST /ingest/actions to reload the entire index. There is no way to upload a single action document through the API without knowing the filesystem layout.

Proposed Solution

Add a new POST /upload/action endpoint that:

  • Accepts a single .md file via multipart/form-data (field name: action)
  • Authenticates with the same X-Admin-Key header as /ingest/actions
  • Sanitizes the filename and persists it to actions/ (overwrites existing files with the same slug)
  • Validates the upload: only .md files, must produce at least one KnowledgeDocument after parsing
  • Calls reload_catalog() to hot-reload the RAG index without restarting the server
  • Returns the saved slug, document count, and endpoint count

Design

  • Route: POST /upload/action (registered on the admin router)
  • Auth: X-Admin-Key header, same as existing admin endpoints
  • Request: multipart/form-data with a single file field action
  • Response: 200 with {slug, saved_to, documents_loaded, endpoints_loaded}
  • Errors: 401 (invalid/missing key), 422 (non-md, empty, unparseable), 500 (disk/reload failure)

Acceptance Criteria

  • Upload a valid .md → 200, file persisted in actions/, RAG index reloaded
  • File is retrievable via /chat immediately after upload
  • Auth required — anonymous requests return 401
  • Non-.md files rejected with 422
  • Empty/unparseable files rejected with 422
  • Duplicate slugs overwrite existing files
  • Full test suite passes (pytest tests/)
  • Add python-multipart dependency (required by FastAPI for file uploads)

Implementation Plan

See: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-action-upload.md

issues.display_title: Issue #3: Segregate Base Knowledge and Uploaded Actions for RAG
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Currently, the system mixes standard GoThru base knowledge with user-uploaded custom actions inside the same actions/ directory. Git tracking uploaded files becomes complicated, and base system knowledge cannot be safely segregated.

Proposed Solution

Separate RAG knowledge into two distinct directories:

  • A new base-knowledge/ directory for the system's baseline RAG .md documents.
  • Keep the existing actions/ directory solely as a destination for the POST /upload/action endpoint.
    Both directories will be aggregated by the RAG loader.

Design

  • Configuration: Add base_knowledge_dir to app/core/config.py in addition to actions_dir.
  • Loader: Modify load_action_documents in app/ingestion/action_loader.py to accept multiple paths and aggregate the KnowledgeDocument results.
  • RAG Engine Initialization: Provide both directories to the loader during startup (routes_chat.py) and ingestion endpoints (routes_admin.py).
  • File System: Move existing .md files to base-knowledge/. Ignore the actions/ folder via .gitignore to prevent uploaded files from entering version control.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Base RAG knowledge moved completely to base-knowledge/.
  • actions/ folder ignored by Git.
  • RAG system startup and /ingest/actions loads files from both directories.
  • /upload/action endpoint persists files only into actions/ and reloads correctly.
  • Full test suite passes (pytest tests/).

Implementation Plan

Implementation already completed via RAG Copilot CLI based on standard plan template.

issues.display_title: Issue #5: Delete Endpoint for Uploaded Actions
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The system can upload custom .md action documents via POST /upload/action, but there is no mechanism to remove these files once they are no longer needed or if they were uploaded incorrectly.

Proposed Solution

Add a new DELETE /upload/action/{slug} endpoint that allows an authenticated admin to remove an uploaded .md action document from the system and automatically refresh the RAG knowledge index.

Design

  • Route: DELETE /upload/action/{slug} (registered on the admin router)
  • Auth: X-Admin-Key header, same as existing admin endpoints
  • Behavior: Unlinks the specific .md file from actions/ based on the slug format.
  • Refresh: Automatically triggers load_action_documents and routes_chat.reload_catalog to update RAG without restart.
  • Response: 200 with {slug, status: "deleted"}
  • Errors: 401 (invalid/missing key), 404 (action file not found), 500 (disk remove or reload failure)

Acceptance Criteria

  • DELETE request with authentic key removes the corresponding .md file from actions/
  • RAG index is updated immediately after the successful file deletion
  • Auth required — anonymous requests return 401
  • Attempting to delete an unknown slug returns 404
  • Automated tests created inside test_upload_action.py to cover deletion logic
  • All tests pass

Implementation Plan

Implementation completed via Kimi Code AI Agent.

issues.display_title: Issue #7: Admin API Key Security, Validation, and Tooling
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Currently, ADMIN_API_KEY is loaded directly as a string from environment variables without validation or management tooling:

  • If unconfigured or empty, admin endpoints return a 503 error without helpful setup guidance or CLI tooling to generate a secure key.
  • There is no startup validation or minimum entropy/length check when running in production environments.
  • There is no rate limiting or brute-force protection on the X-Admin-Key header authentication.

Proposed Solution

Enhance security and developer experience around ADMIN_API_KEY:

  • Provide a CLI helper command or script (e.g. python -m app.core.security generate-key) to generate cryptographically secure keys (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)).
  • Add validation during settings initialization: enforce or warn if ADMIN_API_KEY is too short or insecure when not in development environment.
  • Document best practices for key generation, configuration, and rotation in docs/ or README.md.

Design

  • Security Utility: Add a key generation utility using Python's secrets module.
  • Config Validation: In app/core/config.py, validate admin_api_key length and complexity when app_environment == "production".
  • Safe Feedback: Ensure 401 / 503 responses remain opaque and never leak secret expectations or system paths.

Acceptance Criteria

  • CLI/utility available to generate a secure random admin key
  • Minimum key length validation/warning in production mode
  • Documentation updated in README or docs/ explaining how to set up and rotate ADMIN_API_KEY
  • Existing admin authentication behavior remains backward-compatible
  • Automated tests for config validation and key generation utility

Result

  • Implemented CLI key generator tool (python -m app.core.security generate-key) generating cryptographic keys (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)).
  • Added settings validation in app/core/config.py enforcing minimum 32-character ADMIN_API_KEY length in production environment.
  • Updated README.md with guidelines on generating, configuring, and rotating admin API keys.
  • Added comprehensive unit tests in tests/core/test_security_and_config.py.
  • Merged via PR #13.

issues.display_title: Issue #8: Enhancement: Upload Action Granular Validation and Overwrite Control
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The current POST /actions endpoint has usability and reliability limitations:

  1. Implicit Overwriting: The endpoint automatically and silently overwrites existing action documents with the same slug. There is no protection against accidental overwrites or option to reject/confirm before replacing an existing action.
  2. Orphan Files on 503 / Failure: When an upload request fails with HTTP 503 (e.g. unconfigured service, reload failure, or downstream error), the .md file can end up already written to the actions/ directory without proper cleanup/rollback, leaving behind orphan files in the filesystem.

Proposed Solution

Enhance POST /actions with overwrite protection and strict cleanup:

  • Overwrite Flag / Guard: Add an optional overwrite: bool = True parameter (or query param/form field) that returns 409 Conflict if the file already exists and overwrite is explicitly disabled (overwrite=false).
  • Guaranteed Cleanup / Rollback on 503 & Failures: Ensure that if any step fails (including 503 Service Unavailable, ingestion failure, or reload error), newly created files are strictly removed and existing files restored so no orphan .md file remains in actions/.

Design

  • Route: POST /actions
  • Parameters:
    • action: UploadFile (multipart)
    • overwrite: bool = Form(True)
  • Error Responses:
    • 409 Conflict: Return conflict when overwrite=False and actions/{slug}.md already exists.
    • 503 / 500 Failures: Ensure any failure guarantees rollback/cleanup of the uploaded file.
  • Rollback: Strengthen atomic write and restore mechanism so that no .md remains in actions/ on failure.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Overwrite flag honored: setting overwrite=false on an existing slug returns 409 Conflict without modifying the file
  • On 503 (or any other failure during reload/persistence), ensure uploaded file does not remain in actions/
  • Default behavior remains backward compatible
  • Automated tests added to tests/api/test_upload_action.py for overwrite guards and 503 cleanup verification

Result

  • Added overwrite parameter (bool = Form(True)) to POST /actions returning 409 Conflict if the action already exists and overwrite=False.
  • Implemented robust atomic rollback and cleanup preventing orphan .md files in actions/ when 503/500 reload errors occur.
  • Maintained backward compatibility for existing upload clients (overwrite=True by default).
  • Added comprehensive unit tests in tests/api/test_upload_action.py.
  • Merged via PR #14.

issues.display_title: Issue #15: feat: add context history support for chat and suggest-action
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The /chat and /suggest-action endpoints previously operated in a purely stateless manner per request without conversational memory:

  1. Stateless Prompting: Follow-up questions (e.g., "what's the next step?", "how do I rename it?") were sent to the LLM without prior conversation turns, leading to disconnected or ambiguous responses.
  2. Retrieval Misses on Follow-ups: Short or context-dependent user follow-ups often failed keyword and BM25 document retrieval because essential entity/subject names were only mentioned in earlier conversation turns.
  3. No Standardized Context History Handling: There was no normalization for conversation history payloads supplied in request.context (such as varying key names like history or messages, or different role naming conventions).

Proposed Solution

Introduce conversation context history support to /chat and /suggest-action:

  • Parse and normalize conversation history from request.context supporting history or messages list formats with common role aliases (human, client, sender, bot, ai, etc.).
  • Inject formatted conversation history into the LLM provider prompts to maintain conversational continuity.
  • Implement a retrieval fallback mechanism using the previous user message from history concatenated with the current message when initial retrieval yields no matching documents.
  • Expand retriever stop words to filter common conversational phrasing and avoid false-positive retrieval scoring.

Design

  • History Normalization & Extraction (app/copilot/history.py):
    • normalize_role(role: Any) -> str: Normalizes diverse role aliases into standard roles (User, Assistant, System).
    • extract_chat_history(context: dict[str, Any] | None, limit: int = 10) -> list[dict[str, str]]: Safely extracts and validates recent turns from history or messages, capped at 10 items.
    • format_chat_history(history: list[dict[str, str]]) -> str: Formats turns into Role: Content blocks.
    • get_last_user_message_from_history(history: list[dict[str, str]]) -> str | None: Locates the most recent User utterance for query expansion.
  • Endpoints (app/api/routes_chat.py & app/api/routes_actions.py):
    • Triggers fallback retrieval ("{last_user_msg} {request.message}") if initial document search returns empty and history is present in context.
    • Passes context=request.context to AnswerComposer.compose().
  • LLM Prompting (app/copilot/answerer.py):
    • Injects formatted conversation history into the prompt when present, instructing the model to maintain conversational continuity while remaining grounded in retrieved evidence.
  • Retriever (app/rag/retriever.py):
    • Expanded _STOP_WORDS set to ignore common conversational and auxiliary words.

Sample Payloads

1. Request with Standard History (context.history)

{
  "message": "lalu bagaimana langkah berikutnya?",
  "context": {
    "history": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "How do I unarchive a tour from Google?"
      },
      {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "Open the tour list and click unarchive."
      }
    ]
  },
  "provider": "openai"
}

2. Request with Alternative Messages Format & Aliases (context.messages)

{
  "message": "can you guide me through it step by step?",
  "context": {
    "messages": [
      {
        "sender": "human",
        "text": "How do I rename my tour in GoThru?"
      },
      {
        "role": "bot",
        "message": "You can rename your tour directly from GoThru Dashboard."
      }
    ]
  }
}

3. Response Example (POST /chat & POST /suggest-action)

{
  "mode": "answer_only",
  "answer": "1. Open GoThru Dashboard.\n2. Go to **My Tours**.\n3. Locate the tour you want to rename and click **Edit**.\n4. Update the title in the tour settings and save.",
  "knowledge_sources": [
    "actions/how-to-rename-your-tours-in-gothru.md"
  ],
  "action_plan": {
    "mode": "answer_only",
    "suggested_action": null,
    "reason": null,
    "required_params": [],
    "missing_params": [],
    "confirmation_required": false,
    "api_candidate": null,
    "api_candidates": [],
    "planned_steps": [],

  },
  "debug": {
    "answer_source": "provider",
    "provider_used": "openai",

    "provider_base_url": null
  }
}

Acceptance Criteria

  • Parse and normalize conversation history from request.context supporting history and messages keys
  • Normalize diverse role naming conventions (user, human, client, assistant, bot, ai)
  • Limit parsed history to the most recent 10 turns to avoid prompt token overflow
  • Fallback retrieval using prior user message when follow-up query yields no documents
  • Include conversation history in the LLM prompt with continuity instructions
  • Unit and integration tests for history parsing, prompt formatting, and chat route fallback
  • All test suites pass

Result

  • Implemented app/copilot/history.py with role normalization, history extraction, formatting, and last user message retrieval.
  • Integrated history extraction and contextual prompting into app/copilot/answerer.py.
  • Added retrieval fallback in POST /chat and POST /suggest-action using prior user query when direct document matches are empty.
  • Expanded stop words in app/rag/retriever.py to optimize keyword matching.
  • Added comprehensive unit and integration tests in tests/copilot/test_history.py, tests/copilot/test_answerer.py, and tests/api/test_chat_routes.py.
  • Fixed flaky tampered token test in tests/executor/test_confirmer.py.
  • Merged via PR #16.
